targetAudience.primary: Open-source maintainers and platform engineers implementing OAuth clients, token providers and headless authentication recovery
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands access-token refresh, local credential persistence and exception handling.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A broad catch can silently classify local persistence failure as remote refresh failure, hiding that the authorization server may already have advanced credential state.

whyNow: A same-day merged MCP TypeScript SDK change moves token persistence outside the guarded refresh catch, propagates saveTokens rejection and adds regression coverage for persistence failure without redirect.

externalHook.description: The remote server can issue new credentials successfully while the client fails to durably save them, leaving the two sides at different commit points.

coreProposition: OAuth refresh should be modeled as a split-commit workflow whenever remote credential issuance and local durable persistence are separate operations; persistence failure after remote success is a distinct partial-success state that must remain visible for reconciliation.

originalValue.description: Interprets refresh and persistence as a split-commit boundary, separating exchange failure, persistence failure, deliberate reauthorization and recovery completion instead of collapsing them into one authentication error.

readerTakeaway: Expose which side committed, propagate persistence faults, retain safe recovery evidence, and define retry or operator reconciliation separately from the remote refresh exchange.

supported: The pre-change path grouped refreshAuthorization and saveTokens under one catch.
The merged change keeps only the remote refresh call in the guarded refresh block and lets saveTokens rejection propagate.
A regression test forces disk-full persistence failure after new tokens are returned and verifies that redirect is not called.
Genuine refresh errors remain differentiated and deliberate reauthorization paths gain warnings.
uncertain: How providers should advertise durability and atomic replace
Which non-secret recovery metadata a structured partial-success error should carry

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article concerns a general external-state and local-persistence reliability boundary.

decisionReason: The code change gives direct failure-path evidence, and the Research Object contributes a transferable split-commit model with explicit limits.
